records.name: Cost/Noise
records.definition: The degree to which collecting more telemetry adds cost and noise that can obscure the signals that matter.

records.name: Incident Diagnosis
records.definition: The ability to diagnose the cause of an incident from a system's observable signals.

records.name: Logs

distinctFrom.reason: Logs record discrete events, while traces record the path and timing of one request across components.

records.definition: A record of discrete, timestamped events a system emits about what it did.

records.name: Traces
records.definition: A record of the path and timing of a request as it moves through a system's components.

records.name: Incident Analysis
records.definition: The ability to reconstruct and analyze an incident from the events a system logged.

records.name: Noise/Personal Data Leakage
records.definition: The degree to which verbose logging adds noise and risks leaking personal or sensitive data.

records.name: Structured Events
records.definition: Log entries emitted as structured, machine-parsable records rather than free-form text.

records.name: Alert Noise
records.definition: The degree to which monitoring many signals generates alerts that drown out the meaningful ones.

records.name: Blind Operation
records.definition: Running a system in production with no monitoring, so problems are noticed only when users report them.

records.name: Failure Detection
records.definition: The ability to detect that a system has failed or degraded by watching its monitored signals.

records.name: Alert Fatigue
records.definition: The degree to which too many alerts desensitize responders, so the ones that matter are ignored.

records.name: Incident Response
records.definition: Detecting, triaging, and resolving an operational incident once an alert fires.

records.name: Timely Intervention
records.definition: The ability to intervene on a problem quickly by being alerted the moment it arises.

records.name: Accountability
records.definition: The ability to attribute every consequential action to the actor responsible for it.

records.name: Opaque Mutation
records.definition: Changing state with no record of who changed what or when, so the change cannot be audited.

records.name: Storage/Privacy
records.definition: The degree to which retaining a full audit history grows storage and raises privacy concerns.

records.name: Action

distinctFrom.reason: The action field names the operation, while the target field names the resource it was performed on.
The action field names the operation, while the timestamp field marks when it happened.

records.definition: A field of an audit record identifying the operation that was performed.

records.name: Actor

distinctFrom.reason: The actor field names who acted, while the action field names what was done.
The actor field names who acted, while the target field names what was acted on.
The actor field names who acted, while the timestamp field marks when.

records.definition: A field of an audit record identifying who or what performed an action.

records.name: Forensics
records.definition: The ability to reconstruct after the fact what happened from an immutable audit record.

records.name: Privacy
records.definition: The degree to which a system limits the collection and exposure of personal or sensitive information.

records.name: Target
records.definition: A field of an audit record identifying the resource an action was performed on.

records.name: Timestamp

distinctFrom.reason: The timestamp field marks when an action happened, while the target field names what it was performed on.

records.definition: A field of an audit record marking when an action occurred.

records.name: Untracked Mutation
records.definition: Mutating state without writing an audit entry, so the change leaves no trace.

records.name: Anonymous Flow
records.definition: Data or requests flowing through a system with no identifiers, so their path cannot be reconstructed.

records.name: End-to-End Causality
records.definition: The ability to follow a request's cause-and-effect chain across every component it touches.

records.name: Logs/Traces
records.definition: The combined log and trace records that let a request be followed from end to end.

records.name: Metadata Propagation Overhead
records.definition: The degree to which carrying trace metadata through every call adds size and processing cost.

records.name: Context Propagation
records.definition: The requirement that request context be carried across service boundaries so related calls can be correlated.

records.name: Header/Metadata Management
records.definition: The degree to which threading correlation identifiers through headers adds handling to every call.

records.name: Request-Level Traceability
records.definition: The ability to trace all work belonging to one request by a shared correlation identifier.

records.name: Uncorrelated Events
records.definition: Emitting events with no shared identifier, so those belonging to one request cannot be tied together.

records.name: Audit Trail
records.definition: A chronological record linking each event to the one that caused it.

records.name: Cause-Effect Reconstruction
records.definition: The ability to reconstruct which event triggered which by following causation identifiers.

records.name: Event Metadata
records.definition: Descriptive fields attached to an event, such as its identifiers, timestamps, and causation links.

records.name: Metadata Verbosity
records.definition: The degree to which stamping every event with causation metadata makes the event payload verbose.

records.name: Unlinked Events
records.definition: Recording events with no link to their cause, so cause-and-effect chains cannot be rebuilt.

records.name: Latency/Failure Root Cause Analysis
records.definition: The ability to pinpoint which service caused a request's latency or failure by tracing it across hops.

records.name: Opaque Distributed Calls
records.definition: Calls crossing service boundaries with no tracing, so a request's path and bottlenecks are invisible.

records.name: Overhead/Sampling
records.definition: The degree to which tracing every request adds overhead, forcing sampling that can miss rare cases.

records.name: Trace Context Propagation
records.definition: The requirement that trace identifiers be propagated across every hop of a distributed request.

records.name: Error-Budget Decisions
records.definition: The ability to decide how much risk to take by spending against a defined reliability error budget.

records.name: Feature Velocity
records.definition: The degree to which holding to strict reliability targets limits how fast new features can ship.

records.name: Vague Reliability Goals
records.definition: Stating reliability aims in vague, unmeasurable terms, so no check can tell whether they are met.

records.name: At-a-Glance System Health

distinctFrom.reason: At-a-glance health shows the state now, while trend visibility shows how a metric has moved over time.

records.definition: The ability to see a system's overall health at a glance from a consolidated visual display.

records.name: Dashboard Sprawl
records.definition: The degree to which unchecked creation of dashboards scatters attention across too many redundant views.

records.name: Log-Grep-Only Diagnosis
records.definition: Diagnosing problems solely by grepping raw logs, with no aggregated view of system health.

records.name: Trend Visibility
records.definition: The ability to see how a metric is trending over time from a visualized history.

records.name: Structured Log
records.definition: A technique for writing log entries as typed fields, so they are queried by field instead of by text.

records.name: Trace Span
records.definition: A technique for recording the start, end and context of an operation as a span within a request's trace.

records.name: Alert on Critical Failure
records.definition: A technique for raising an alert with an owner and a severity when a critical path fails.

records.name: Cardinality Reduction
records.definition: A technique for limiting the distinct label values a metric carries, so its storage and queries stay bounded.

records.name: Sampling and Aggregation
records.definition: A technique for keeping a representative share of telemetry or a summary of it instead of every event.

records.name: Runbook Owner
records.definition: A technique for naming the person or team responsible for each alert and its response steps.

records.name: Causation Tracing
records.definition: A technique for carrying the id of the event or request that caused each effect, so a chain can be followed back.

records.name: Usage Instrumentation
records.definition: A technique for counting calls to a code path in production, so its use is measured before it is removed.

records.name: Data Change Audit
records.definition: A technique for recording who changed which data, when, and from what value to what value.

records.name: Execution Log
records.definition: A technique for recording each step an automated or manual procedure performed and its result.

records.name: Define Signal Quality
records.definition: A technique for stating what makes a log, metric or alert useful before it is emitted.

records.name: Service Level Objectives
records.definition: A technique for choosing measured indicators of reliability and setting the targets a service must meet on them.
